summary: Daidō Moriyama is a Japanese photographer known for his black-and-white street photography and association with the avant-garde magazine Provoke. His work, including photobooks like Japan: A Photo Theater and Farewell Photography, captures the rawness of postwar urban life. He has produced over 150 photobooks and received major awards such as the Hasselblad Award in 2019.

claims.text: Daidō Moriyama was born on October 10, 1938 in Ikeda, Osaka, Japan.
Moriyama has produced more than 150 photobooks since 1968.
claims.evidence_quote: he has produced more than 150 photobooks since 1968

claims.text: Moriyama received the Hasselblad Award in 2019.
Moriyama's work is associated with the 'are, bure, boke' style, meaning 'grainy/rough, blurry, out-of-focus'.
claims.evidence_quote: The publication popularized the "are, bure, boke" style, translated as "grainy/rough, blurry, out-of-focus"

claims.text: Moriyama photographed Kanye West's album cover for 'Bully' (2026).
claims.evidence_quote: In 2024, he photographed American rapper Kanye West's cover for his studio album Bully (2026).

claims.text: Moriyama's photobook 'Farewell Photography' (1972) takes a nihilistic turn, focusing on the incidental and evocative nature of photography.
claims.evidence_quote: The photobook, as suggested by the title, takes a nihilistic turn from his prior work, turning its attention towards the incidental and evocative nature of photography rather than the visual subject itself.

claims.text: Moriyama's 'Accident' series (1969) was prompted by seeing news of Robert F. Kennedy's assassination on newspapers at a train terminal.
claims.evidence_quote: the series was prompted by an experience he had at a train terminal in Tokyo, whereupon he was shocked to see the news of Robert F. Kennedy's assassination on the front page of newspapers scattered all around him.

claims.text: Moriyama often captures images without looking through the viewfinder.
claims.evidence_quote: Moriyama tends to capture images without looking through the viewfinder

claims.text: Moriyama has been shooting with color since the 1970s and since the late 2000s works almost exclusively with compact digital photography.
claims.evidence_quote: he has been shooting with color since the 1970s, and since the late 2000s has turned increasingly to compact digital photography, now working almost exclusively in this medium.

claims.text: Moriyama helped establish the Workshop Photography School in 1974 with Shōmei Tōmatsu.
claims.evidence_quote: In 1974 Moriyama helped Shōmei Tōmatsu to establish the Workshop Photography School
